A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 27-page versions of Polychromic Objectives for Reinforcement Learning. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original BabyAI, MiniGrid and Triangle Discovery experiments, including reward, success, diversity and generalization results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical evaluations, including Tables 1–2, Figures 2–4 and the perturbation examples in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The implemented polychromic objective, vine sampling, shared advantages, PPO updates and window mechanism remain unchanged in Sections 3.2–3.3 and Appendix A. The revised definition of set RL does not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four BabyAI tasks, MiniGrid Four Rooms and Algorithmic Creativity Triangle Discovery, including the same initial-state perturbation scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same pretrained-policy, REINFORCE-with-baseline and PPO comparisons, with the same UCB variants in the grid environments. The newly cited Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning work is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The data splits, 50 grid configurations, graph selection, reward definitions, metrics and training settings are unchanged. Both versions retain the 136-trajectory budget and the perturbation protocol using 100 exploratory rollouts and 10 starting positions per visited room.

E4.justification: The pass@k diversity analyses, initial-state robustness experiment and Figure 6 trajectory examples are retained. Appendix A's observations about KL stabilization and the polychromic window are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains averaging across three random seeds. Neither version adds or changes repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-reporting practices relative to the other.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–4 retain their values, curves and findings. For example, Poly-PPO's Goto reward and success remain 0.575 and 80.2%, and its perturbed-state pass rate remains 60.6%.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a formal irreducibility condition: set RL excludes objectives expressible, for every policy, as an expectation of a single-trajectory function independent of policy parameters. This narrows v2's formulation, which explicitly included mean return. Existing derivations and Appendix C proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same headline contributions and claims: polychromic objectives and a PPO adaptation that preserve diverse successful behaviors, improve pass@k coverage and generalize under perturbations.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly qualifies when set-level optimization is essential, explaining that merely averaging returns reduces to standard RL and connecting irreducible objectives to dependence between evaluated trajectories. Experimental interpretations and the limitations in Section 7 are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same architectures, preprocessing, reward construction, sampling details, hyperparameters and full pseudocode. No implementation or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Tajwar, Zeng et al. (2026), Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning, when discussing connections between RL and maximum likelihood estimation. The existing related-work coverage and comparisons otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 expands the Section 3.1 explanation and makes limited wording and acknowledgment edits while retaining the section structure. It also corrects the printed coefficient in Lemma 5.3 from lambda to lambda-prime, matching the existing Appendix C.3 statement.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their content and designs. Figure 2 moves upward on page 7, other displays shift with text reflow, and citations and cross-references become blue. There is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the distinction between irreducible set objectives and ordinary expected-return objectives more precise, and resolves the notation mismatch between Lemma 5.3 and Appendix C.3. These improve conceptual clarity and internal consistency. The empirical evidence, implemented method and substantive limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
